Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verses 1–6:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿By those that scatter, scattering (1), and those that bear a burden, (2) and those that run with ease, (3) and those that distribute by command, (4) Surely what you are promised is true (5), and surely the Judgment is bound to come (6)﴾

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿By those that scatter, scattering﴾: meaning, by the winds that scatter the dust, scattering. It is said: the wind scattered (dharat) the dust and it scattered (adharat) it.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn Arfaja, who said: A man stood up before Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: What are "those that scatter, scattering"? He said: They are the winds.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, who said: I heard Khalid ibn Arfaja say: I heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, when he had gone out to the open square (al-Rahba), wearing two cloaks. They said: If only a man would ask and the people would hear. So Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up and said: What are "those that scatter, scattering"? He said: They are the winds.

- Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ubayd al-Hilali and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, they said: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthmah narrated to us, he said: Musa ibn Ya'qub al-Zam'i narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Huwayrith narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who informed him, he said: I heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, addressing the people, and Abd Allah ibn al-Kawwa' stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, inform me about the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿By those that scatter, scattering﴾. He said: They are the winds.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about "those that scatter, scattering", and he said: The wind.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ali: ﴿By those that scatter, scattering﴾, he said: The wind.

Mihran said: It was related to us from Simak, from Khalid ibn Arfaja, who said: I asked Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, about ﴿By those that scatter, scattering﴾, and he said: The wind.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who said: I heard Abu al-Tufayl say: I heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, say: Let them not ask me about a speaking Book or an established Sunnah without my informing you. Then Ibn al-Kawwa' asked him about "those that scatter", and he said: They are the winds.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Talq narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Asim, from Ali ibn Rabi'ah, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa' asked Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, saying: ﴿By those that scatter, scattering﴾, and he said: The wind.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Rafi', from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa' said to Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: What are "those that scatter, scattering"? He said: The wind.

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to me, from Abu Sakhrah, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said while on the pulpit: No one will ask me about a verse of the Book of Allah without my informing him. Then Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up, wishing to ask him what Sabigh had asked Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: What are "those that scatter, scattering"? Ali said: The winds.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that a man asked Ali about "those that scatter", and he said: They are the winds.

- Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Wahb ibn Abd Allah, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa' asked Ali, saying: What are "those that scatter, scattering"? He said: The winds.

- Yunus narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿By those that scatter, scattering﴾: Ibn Abbas used to say: They are the winds.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿By those that scatter﴾, he said: The winds.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and those that bear a burden﴾:

It means: the clouds that carry their burden of water.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and those that run with ease﴾:

It means: the ships that run upon the seas with ease and facility. ﴿And those that distribute by command﴾: it means the angels who distribute the command of Allah among His creation.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Hannad narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn Arfaja, who said: A man stood up before Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: What are "those that run with ease"? He said: They are the ships. He said: Then what are "those that bear a burden"? He said: They are the clouds. He said: Then what are "those that distribute by command"? He said: They are the angels.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, who said: I heard Khalid ibn Arfaja say: I heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and he was asked: What are "those that bear a burden"? He said: They are the clouds. He said: Then what are "those that run with ease"? He said: They are the ships. He said: Then what are "those that distribute by command"? He said: They are the angels.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from Khalid ibn Arfaja, from Ali, similarly.

- Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ubayd Allah al-Hilali and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, they said: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthmah narrated to us, he said: Musa al-Zam'i narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Huwayrith narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who informed him, he said: I heard Ali addressing the people, and Abd Allah ibn al-Kawwa' stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, inform me about the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿and those that bear a burden﴾. He said: They are the clouds. ﴿and those that run with ease﴾. He said: They are the ships. ﴿and those that distribute by command﴾. He said: The angels.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who said: I heard Abu al-Tufayl say: I heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and he mentioned something similar.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi', from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa' said to Ali, and he mentioned something similar.

- Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Wahb ibn Abd Allah, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: I witnessed Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up before him, and he mentioned something similar.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Asim, from Ali ibn Rabi'ah, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa' asked Ali, and he mentioned something similar.

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to me, from Abu Sakhr, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, similarly.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that a man asked Ali, and he mentioned something similar.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ali, the like of it.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: He was asked, and he mentioned the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying ﴿and those that bear a burden﴾: He said: The clouds. Regarding his saying ﴿and those that distribute by command﴾: He said: The angels.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and those that bear a burden﴾, he said: The clouds carrying the rain. ﴿and those that run with ease﴾, he said: The ships. ﴿and those that distribute by command﴾, he said: The angels who bring it down by His command upon whomever He wills.

* *

His saying ﴿Surely what you are promised is true﴾:

It means: Verily what you are promised, O people, of the establishment of the Hour and the resurrection of the dead from their graves, is true; that is, it is a reality of certain truth.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Surely what you are promised is true﴾: And the meaning is "truthfulness" (lasidq), so the noun was put in place of the verbal noun. ﴿And surely the Judgment is bound to come﴾: meaning, the reckoning, the reward and the punishment are indeed due, and Allah will recompense His servants for their deeds.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Surely what you are promised is true and surely the Judgment is bound to come﴾: That is the Day of Resurrection, the Day on which people will be judged for their deeds.

- Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and surely the Judgment is bound to come﴾: He said: The Day on which Allah will judge His servants for their deeds.

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and surely the Judgment is bound to come﴾: He said: Certainly occurring.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verses 7–9:

The explanation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿By the sky full of paths (7). Indeed, you are in conflicting speech (8). Turned away from it is whoever is turned away (9).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "By the sky possessing good creation." By His saying ﴿dhat al-hubuk﴾ ("full of paths") He means: possessing paths. The "hubuk" of anything is its folds and creases; it is the plural of "hibak" and "habika." It is said of the crinkled hair's waves that they are "hubuk," and of sand when the still wind passes over it, of standing water, and of an iron coat of mail that it has "hubuk." From this is the verse of the rajaz poet:

"As if the weaver had draped over her a carpet, with patterns woven into it and hibak,
Its movement and its swift running have made it shine."[[The rajaz poet describes the back of a wild female ass, which has patterns, markings, lines and paths, as though a weaver had woven it. He has dressed her in a patterned carpet with straight, colored lines. The meaning of the third verse: the lines on her back shine as though gilded when she moves and keeps pace in her march. The point of evidence in these verses is his saying "hibak." The hibak is a line in sand, in cloth, or in hair, and its plural is "hubuk" with two damma. Similarly "habika," whose plural is "habaik." The author cited these three verses of the shortened rajaz meter when discussing His saying "and the sky full of hubuk." It refers to the streaks of light seen in the sky when the moon is absent, which are called the Milky Way; or it refers to the spheres in which the stars revolve. The third verse came in the original corrupted thus: "Adhhabaha al-huquq al-din al-dak." We searched for it extensively, did not find it, and then corrected it as you see. "Al-khufuq" means movement and agitation; "al-darak" means continuous running.]]

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said, although the wording of those who said it differs.

Those who said this:

Abu Husayn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: ʿAbthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, he said: "possessing good creation."

He said: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿid ibn Masruq, brother of Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, he said: "possessing adornment."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Bazi narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, he said: "it was made full with good creation, it was made full with stars."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, he said: "it was made full with good creation, it was made full with stars."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn al-Haytham narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, he said: "possessing good creation, it was made full with stars."

Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: ʿImran ibn Hudayr narrated to us, saying: ʿIkrimah was asked about His saying ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, and he said: "possessing good creation. Have you not seen the weaver when he weaves a garment? [He] says: how beautifully he has made its hubuk."

Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from a man among the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, behind you is the deceiving misleader, and indeed his head behind him is hubuk, hubuk." By "al-hubuk" he means: curliness.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, he said: "its evenness: its beauty."

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, he said: "possessing good creation."

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, who said: "Its hubuk are its stars." And Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: "﴿al-hubuk﴾: possessing good creation."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾: "that is, possessing good creation." And al-Hasan used to say: "its hubuk: its stars."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, ﴿dhat al-hubuk﴾, he said: "possessing good creation."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, he said: "firmly constructed structure."

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾: "possessing adornment." And it is also said: "its hubuk is like the hubuk of sand, and like the hubuk of a coat of mail, and like the hubuk of water when the wind strikes it, so it is woven into paths."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿dhat al-hubuk﴾: "al-shiddah (strength): hubuka means shuddat (was strengthened)." And he recited the saying of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿And We built above you seven strong [heavens]﴾.

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿and the sky full of hubuk﴾, he said: "possessing good creation; and it is said: possessing adornment."

His mention, exalted is He, means: cursed are the soothsayers who speculate falsehood and vanity, conjecturing it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning those meant by His words ﴿Destroyed are the liars﴾. Some of them said: it refers to the doubters.

One group said: he is only a sorcerer, and what he brought is sorcery. Another group said: he is only a poet, and what he brought is poetry. Another group said: he is only a soothsayer, and what he brought is soothsaying. And another group said ﴿Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, so they are dictated to him morning and evening﴾, fabricating against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

His mention, exalted is He, means: cursed are the soothsayers who speculate falsehood and vanity, conjecturing it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning those meant by His words ﴿Destroyed are the liars﴾. Some of them said: it refers to the doubters.

His mention, exalted is He, means: those who are persisting in the error of misguidance and its overwhelming them, and who are heedless of the truth with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, having turned away from it.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said, although their wording in explaining it differed.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verses 14–16:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Taste your trial. This is what you were demanding to hasten.﴾ [51:14] ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be within gardens and springs,﴾ [51:15] ﴿Taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good.﴾ [51:16]

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Taste your trial﴾: it is said to them, "Taste your trial," and the words "and it is said" are omitted, the context indicating them.

By His saying ﴿your trial﴾ is meant your punishment and your burning.

The people of interpretation differed regarding this. Some of them said what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿your trial﴾, he said: your burning.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, ﴿Taste your trial﴾: taste your punishment, ﴿This is what you were demanding to hasten﴾.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he says: the day they are punished, so it is said: taste your punishment.

- I was told by al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he says: your burning.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he says: your burning.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he said: taste your punishment.

Others said: What is meant by that is: taste your torment or your denial.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he says: your denial.

- I was told by al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he says: your burning; and it is said: your denial.

* *

As for His saying ﴿This is what you were demanding to hasten﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: it is said to them, "This is the punishment which you are being given today, and it is the punishment which you were demanding to hasten in the world."

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be within gardens and springs﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: those who feared God by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience in the world will be in gardens and springs of water in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Taking what their Lord has given them﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: acting upon what their Lord commanded them, discharging His obligations.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abu Umar, from Muslim al-Batin, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Taking what their Lord has given them﴾, he said: the obligations.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾:

He says: indeed they were, before the obligations were prescribed upon them, doers of good; he says: they were obedient to God before that.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abu Umar, from Muslim al-Batin, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾, he said: before the obligations, doers of good, acting.
