- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he says: your burning.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he said: taste your punishment.

Others said: What is meant by that is: taste your torment or your denial.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he says: your denial.

- I was told by al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿Taste your trial﴾, he says: your burning; and it is said: your denial.

* *

As for His saying ﴿This is what you were demanding to hasten﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: it is said to them, "This is the punishment which you are being given today, and it is the punishment which you were demanding to hasten in the world."

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be within gardens and springs﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: those who feared God by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience in the world will be in gardens and springs of water in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Taking what their Lord has given them﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: acting upon what their Lord commanded them, discharging His obligations.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abu Umar, from Muslim al-Batin, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Taking what their Lord has given them﴾, he said: the obligations.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾:

He says: indeed they were, before the obligations were prescribed upon them, doers of good; he says: they were obedient to God before that.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abu Umar, from Muslim al-Batin, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾, he said: before the obligations, doers of good, acting.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ (17) ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾ (18) ﴿and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ (19)**

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil, the people of interpretation) differed over the meaning of His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾. Some said: its meaning is, "They used to be awake for little of the night, not sleeping," and they took "mā" (what) to carry the sense of negation.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They would wake up and pray between these two prayers, between Maghrib and 'Isha'."
- Zurayq ibn al-Shahhab narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, similarly.
- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Bukayr ibn Abi al-Samt narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They did not sleep until they had prayed the 'Atamah (night prayer)."
- They both said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Few were the nights that passed over them without their praying in them."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah said regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "Few were the nights that came upon them in which they did not pray to God, either from its beginning or from its middle."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "No night passed over them without their taking some portion of it, even if a little."
- He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "They would attain a portion of it."
- 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They did not sleep between Maghrib and 'Isha'."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam and Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They would attain a portion of the night."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Mutarrif, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Few were the nights that came over them without their sleeping through all of them."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They had little of the night in which they slept; they used to pray it."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Abi Najih say regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "They used to sleep little on any night until morning."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Little did they sleep on a night until morning; they did not perform tahajjud (voluntary night prayer)."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "They used to sleep but little of the night," and they treated the "mā" in His words ﴿mā yahja'ūn (they used to sleep)﴾ as a redundant particle (sila, a particle without independent meaning).

Those who said this include:

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "al-Hasan said: 'They endured the standing (prayer) of the night'."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: "They slept of it only a little."
- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from some of our companions, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They slept of the night only its least portion."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Few were the nights that came over them without their sleeping."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "They did not sleep except a little."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said, reciting this verse ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "I am not of the people of this verse."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "The standing (prayer) of the night."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: "They were energetic, so they extended (their prayer) until the pre-dawn."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "They extended (their) prayer and were energetic, until seeking forgiveness was at pre-dawn."
- He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: "They did not sleep at night except a little."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "al-Hasan and al-Zuhri used to say: 'They used to pray much of the night'." It is also permissible that the "mā" in this interpretation be in the nominative position (marfu', grammatical case), and the sense of the statement would be: "They used to sleep but little of the night, their sleep." As for the one who treats "mā" as a redundant particle, it has no grammatical position; the meaning of the statement according to his view would be "They used to sleep the little of the night," and if "mā" is redundant, then "qalīl" (little) is in the accusative case governed by "yahja'ūn" (they sleep).
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They did not sleep."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "They used to pray the 'Atamah," and in this interpretation, "mā" carries the sense of negation.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "A man from the people of Makkah said, Qatadah named him: the 'Atamah prayer."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: those good-doers were few among people before the obligations were prescribed upon them. They read the statement after His words ﴿Indeed they were before that good-doers﴾ as "They were few," and then began a new sentence with His words ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little﴾. Therefore, "mā" in this interpretation must carry the sense of negation.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He says: "The good-doers were few; then it begins, saying ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾," as He said ﴿And those who believed in God and His messengers, those are the truthful ones﴾, then He said: ﴿And the martyrs with their Lord; for them is their reward and their light﴾.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zubayr, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They were few among the people."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adiyy, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They were few among the people who did that."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adiyy, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They were few among the people at that time."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: "'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: God said ﴿Indeed the righteous are in gardens and springs﴾ ... to ﴿good-doers﴾." He said: "They were few." He means: "The good-doers were few." This is separated, then He resumed, saying ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little﴾.

As for His words ﴿yahja'ūn (they sleep)﴾, it means: they sleep; and al-hujū' (sleeping) is: sleep.

Those who held the view we have stated regarding this, among the interpreters, are:

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He says, "They sleep."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They sleep."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the same.
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little﴾: "al-hujū' (sleep): sleep."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They used to sleep little of the night." He said: "That is al-hajʻ (the dozing). And the Arabs say: 'When you travel, make us doze (ihja' bina) a little.'" He said: A man from the Banu Tamim said to my father: "O Abu Usamah, a description I do not find among us: God, blessed and exalted is He, mentioned a people and said ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾, and we, by God, stand little of the night." He said: My father said: "Blessed is the one who sleeps when he is drowsy, and whom God meets when he wakes."

The most correct of the interpretations regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ is the view of the one who said: "They used to sleep but little of the night," because God, blessed and exalted is He, described them with that as praise for them and as commendation of them. So describing them with abundance of worship, staying awake through the night, and striving through it in what brings them near to Him and earns His pleasure is more fitting and more appropriate than describing them with little worship and much sleep. And what we have chosen in this is the most prevalent meaning according to the apparent sense of the revelation.

* *

And His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾.

The interpreters differed over its interpretation. Some said: its meaning is: "and at dawn they would pray."

Those who said this include:

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He says, "They would stand and pray." He says: "They used to stand and sleep." As God said to Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿Indeed your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) less than two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it, and a group of those with you﴾. This is sleep and this is standing. ﴿and a group of those with you﴾; likewise they would stand for a third, a half, and two-thirds. He says: they would sleep and they would stand.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He said, "They would pray."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He said, "They would pray."

Others said: Rather, what is meant is that they delayed their seeking forgiveness for their sins until the pre-dawn.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "They extended (their prayer) and were energetic, until seeking forgiveness was at pre-dawn."
- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He said, "They are the believers." He said: "It has reached us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) Ya'qub, when they asked him to seek forgiveness for them, (said) ﴿O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins﴾ — ﴿He said: I will seek forgiveness for you from my Lord﴾." He said: "Some people of knowledge said: he delayed the seeking of forgiveness until the pre-dawn." He said: "And some people of knowledge mentioned that the hour in which the gates of Paradise are opened is the pre-dawn."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say: "al-Sahar (pre-dawn) is the final sixth of the night."

* *

And His words ﴿and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: and in the wealth of these good-doers whose attributes He described there is a right for their beggar, the one who needs what is in their hands, and for the deprived.

The interpreters agreed with what we have said regarding the meaning of "the beggar," but they differed regarding the meaning of "the deprived." One said: it is the one who has been dispossessed (al-mahrūf), who has no share in Islam.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas: I asked him about "the beggar and the deprived," and he said: "The beggar is the one who asks people, and the deprived is the one who has no share in Islam, and he is mahrif (dispossessed)."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: He said: "The deprived: the mahraf (dispossessed)."
- Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The beggar: the beggar. And the deprived: the mahraf who has no share in Islam."
- Sahl ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The deprived: the mahraf who has no share in Islam."
- Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: He said: "The beggar: the one who asks. And the deprived: the mahraf."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Ishaq narrate from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, blessed and exalted is He, "the deprived": He said, "the mahraf."
- And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and the deprived﴾: "He is the man who is mahraf, who has no wealth except that which goes, which God has decreed for him."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His words ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾, and he said: "The beggar: the one who asks. And the deprived: the mahraf who has no share in Islam."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Muqaddami narrated to me, saying: Quraysh ibn Anas narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: "The deprived: the mahraf (dispossessed)."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said regarding "the deprived": "He is the mahraf who has no one to show him kindness or give him anything."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Qilabah, who said: "A flood came in al-Yamamah and took the wealth of a man, so a man from among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'This is the deprived'."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Nafi', who said: "The deprived: the mahraf."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The deprived: the mahraf."
- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, from al-Walid ibn al-'Iza'r, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "The deprived: he is the mahraf."

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 51, verses 17–19 (part 2 of 2)**

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about "the deprived" (al-mahrum), and he did not say anything about it. Then Ata' said: He is the one who is restricted (al-mahdud al-muharif).

Another said: He is the one who abstains (al-muta'affif) and does not ask people for anything.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he was asked about "the deprived," and he said: "the muharif." [[هذا الأثر يناسب القول الأول، فلعله مؤخر من تقديم.]]

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "These are two of the poor of the Muslims: a beggar who asks with his hand, and a poor man who abstains. Both of them have a right over you, O son of Adam."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The beggar is the one who asks, and the deprived is the one who abstains and does not ask."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, saying: Ma'mar said, and al-Zuhri related to me, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one who is turned away by a date or two dates, or a morsel or two morsels." They said: "Then who is the poor man, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who does not find sufficiency, and whose need is not known so that he may be given charity. He is the deprived (al-mahrum)."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The beggar is the one who asks with his hand, and the deprived is the one who abstains. Both of them have a right over you, O son of Adam."

Another said: He is the one who has no share in the spoils of war (al-ghanima).

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent out a military expedition (sariyya), and they took spoils. Then a group came who had witnessed the spoils, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim al-Jadali, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, who said: An expedition was sent out and they took spoils. Then a group came after them, and ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾ was revealed.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, that some people came to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) in Kufa after the Battle of the Camel, and he said: "Distribute to them." He said: "This is the deprived."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, that a people in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) obtained booty, and then a group came later, and ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ was revealed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, saying: Amr related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "The deprived is the one who has no fay' (share of the public revenue) in Islam, and he is restricted (muharif) among the people."

⁕ [He] said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding his saying ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The deprived is the one to whom nothing of the fay' is allotted, and he is restricted (muharif) among the people."

Another said: He is the one whose wealth does not grow.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Husayn, who said: I asked Ikrima about "the beggar and the deprived." He said: "The beggar is the one who asks you, and the deprived is the one whose wealth does not grow."

Another said: He is the one whose fruit and crops have been destroyed.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The deprived is the one whose fruit and crops have been struck by calamity." He recited ﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who make it grow?﴾ … until ﴿Rather, we are deprived (mahrumun)﴾, and the companions of the Garden said: ﴿Indeed, we are astray. Rather, we are deprived﴾.

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding the words of Allah ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "That is not zakat, but it is what they spend from their wealth after paying zakat. The deprived is the one whose crops, fruit, or livestock offspring is struck by calamity, so he has a right over those Muslims who were not struck by that, just as the companions of the Garden said when Allah destroyed their garden: ﴿Rather, we are deprived.﴾" And he also said: ﴿If We willed, We would make it debris, and you would remain astonished. Indeed, we are laden with debt. Rather, we are deprived.﴾

It was al-Sha'bi who would say about this:

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Ibn Awn, who said: al-Sha'bi said: "I am unable to know what the deprived is."

The correct view on this matter, in my judgment, is that the deprived is the one who has been denied provision and is in need. This may be due to the loss of his wealth and crops, so that he becomes among those whom Allah has deprived of that; it may be due to his abstention and his refraining from asking; and it may be because he has no share in the spoils of war because he was absent from the battle. No view is more correct than that it be general, as the Exalted has said: ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ (17) ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾ (18) ﴿and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ (19)**

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil, the people of interpretation) differed over the meaning of His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾. Some said: its meaning is, "They used to be awake for little of the night, not sleeping," and they took "mā" (what) to carry the sense of negation.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They would wake up and pray between these two prayers, between Maghrib and 'Isha'."
- Zurayq ibn al-Shahhab narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, similarly.
- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Bukayr ibn Abi al-Samt narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They did not sleep until they had prayed the 'Atamah (night prayer)."
- They both said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Few were the nights that passed over them without their praying in them."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah said regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "Few were the nights that came upon them in which they did not pray to God, either from its beginning or from its middle."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "No night passed over them without their taking some portion of it, even if a little."
- He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "They would attain a portion of it."
- 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They did not sleep between Maghrib and 'Isha'."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam and Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They would attain a portion of the night."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Mutarrif, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Few were the nights that came over them without their sleeping through all of them."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They had little of the night in which they slept; they used to pray it."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Abi Najih say regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "They used to sleep little on any night until morning."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Little did they sleep on a night until morning; they did not perform tahajjud (voluntary night prayer)."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "They used to sleep but little of the night," and they treated the "mā" in His words ﴿mā yahja'ūn (they used to sleep)﴾ as a redundant particle (sila, a particle without independent meaning).

Those who said this include:

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "al-Hasan said: 'They endured the standing (prayer) of the night'."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: "They slept of it only a little."
- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from some of our companions, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They slept of the night only its least portion."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Few were the nights that came over them without their sleeping."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "They did not sleep except a little."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said, reciting this verse ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "I am not of the people of this verse."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "The standing (prayer) of the night."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: "They were energetic, so they extended (their prayer) until the pre-dawn."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "They extended (their) prayer and were energetic, until seeking forgiveness was at pre-dawn."
- He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: "They did not sleep at night except a little."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "al-Hasan and al-Zuhri used to say: 'They used to pray much of the night'." It is also permissible that the "mā" in this interpretation be in the nominative position (marfu', grammatical case), and the sense of the statement would be: "They used to sleep but little of the night, their sleep." As for the one who treats "mā" as a redundant particle, it has no grammatical position; the meaning of the statement according to his view would be "They used to sleep the little of the night," and if "mā" is redundant, then "qalīl" (little) is in the accusative case governed by "yahja'ūn" (they sleep).
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They did not sleep."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "They used to pray the 'Atamah," and in this interpretation, "mā" carries the sense of negation.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "A man from the people of Makkah said, Qatadah named him: the 'Atamah prayer."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: those good-doers were few among people before the obligations were prescribed upon them. They read the statement after His words ﴿Indeed they were before that good-doers﴾ as "They were few," and then began a new sentence with His words ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little﴾. Therefore, "mā" in this interpretation must carry the sense of negation.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He says: "The good-doers were few; then it begins, saying ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾," as He said ﴿And those who believed in God and His messengers, those are the truthful ones﴾, then He said: ﴿And the martyrs with their Lord; for them is their reward and their light﴾.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zubayr, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They were few among the people."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adiyy, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They were few among the people who did that."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adiyy, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They were few among the people at that time."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: "'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: God said ﴿Indeed the righteous are in gardens and springs﴾ ... to ﴿good-doers﴾." He said: "They were few." He means: "The good-doers were few." This is separated, then He resumed, saying ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little﴾.

As for His words ﴿yahja'ūn (they sleep)﴾, it means: they sleep; and al-hujū' (sleeping) is: sleep.

Those who held the view we have stated regarding this, among the interpreters, are:

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He says, "They sleep."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They sleep."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the same.
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little﴾: "al-hujū' (sleep): sleep."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They used to sleep little of the night." He said: "That is al-hajʻ (the dozing). And the Arabs say: 'When you travel, make us doze (ihja' bina) a little.'" He said: A man from the Banu Tamim said to my father: "O Abu Usamah, a description I do not find among us: God, blessed and exalted is He, mentioned a people and said ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾, and we, by God, stand little of the night." He said: My father said: "Blessed is the one who sleeps when he is drowsy, and whom God meets when he wakes."

The most correct of the interpretations regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ is the view of the one who said: "They used to sleep but little of the night," because God, blessed and exalted is He, described them with that as praise for them and as commendation of them. So describing them with abundance of worship, staying awake through the night, and striving through it in what brings them near to Him and earns His pleasure is more fitting and more appropriate than describing them with little worship and much sleep. And what we have chosen in this is the most prevalent meaning according to the apparent sense of the revelation.

* *

And His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾.

The interpreters differed over its interpretation. Some said: its meaning is: "and at dawn they would pray."

Those who said this include:

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He says, "They would stand and pray." He says: "They used to stand and sleep." As God said to Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿Indeed your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) less than two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it, and a group of those with you﴾. This is sleep and this is standing. ﴿and a group of those with you﴾; likewise they would stand for a third, a half, and two-thirds. He says: they would sleep and they would stand.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He said, "They would pray."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He said, "They would pray."

Others said: Rather, what is meant is that they delayed their seeking forgiveness for their sins until the pre-dawn.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "They extended (their prayer) and were energetic, until seeking forgiveness was at pre-dawn."
- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He said, "They are the believers." He said: "It has reached us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) Ya'qub, when they asked him to seek forgiveness for them, (said) ﴿O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins﴾ — ﴿He said: I will seek forgiveness for you from my Lord﴾." He said: "Some people of knowledge said: he delayed the seeking of forgiveness until the pre-dawn." He said: "And some people of knowledge mentioned that the hour in which the gates of Paradise are opened is the pre-dawn."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say: "al-Sahar (pre-dawn) is the final sixth of the night."

* *

And His words ﴿and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: and in the wealth of these good-doers whose attributes He described there is a right for their beggar, the one who needs what is in their hands, and for the deprived.

The interpreters agreed with what we have said regarding the meaning of "the beggar," but they differed regarding the meaning of "the deprived." One said: it is the one who has been dispossessed (al-mahrūf), who has no share in Islam.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas: I asked him about "the beggar and the deprived," and he said: "The beggar is the one who asks people, and the deprived is the one who has no share in Islam, and he is mahrif (dispossessed)."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: He said: "The deprived: the mahraf (dispossessed)."
- Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The beggar: the beggar. And the deprived: the mahraf who has no share in Islam."
- Sahl ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The deprived: the mahraf who has no share in Islam."
- Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: He said: "The beggar: the one who asks. And the deprived: the mahraf."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Ishaq narrate from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, blessed and exalted is He, "the deprived": He said, "the mahraf."
- And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and the deprived﴾: "He is the man who is mahraf, who has no wealth except that which goes, which God has decreed for him."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His words ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾, and he said: "The beggar: the one who asks. And the deprived: the mahraf who has no share in Islam."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Muqaddami narrated to me, saying: Quraysh ibn Anas narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: "The deprived: the mahraf (dispossessed)."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said regarding "the deprived": "He is the mahraf who has no one to show him kindness or give him anything."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Qilabah, who said: "A flood came in al-Yamamah and took the wealth of a man, so a man from among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'This is the deprived'."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Nafi', who said: "The deprived: the mahraf."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The deprived: the mahraf."
- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, from al-Walid ibn al-'Iza'r, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "The deprived: he is the mahraf."

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 51, verses 17–19 (part 2 of 2)**

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about "the deprived" (al-mahrum), and he did not say anything about it. Then Ata' said: He is the one who is restricted (al-mahdud al-muharif).

Another said: He is the one who abstains (al-muta'affif) and does not ask people for anything.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he was asked about "the deprived," and he said: "the muharif." [[هذا الأثر يناسب القول الأول، فلعله مؤخر من تقديم.]]

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "These are two of the poor of the Muslims: a beggar who asks with his hand, and a poor man who abstains. Both of them have a right over you, O son of Adam."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The beggar is the one who asks, and the deprived is the one who abstains and does not ask."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, saying: Ma'mar said, and al-Zuhri related to me, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one who is turned away by a date or two dates, or a morsel or two morsels." They said: "Then who is the poor man, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who does not find sufficiency, and whose need is not known so that he may be given charity. He is the deprived (al-mahrum)."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The beggar is the one who asks with his hand, and the deprived is the one who abstains. Both of them have a right over you, O son of Adam."

Another said: He is the one who has no share in the spoils of war (al-ghanima).

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent out a military expedition (sariyya), and they took spoils. Then a group came who had witnessed the spoils, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim al-Jadali, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, who said: An expedition was sent out and they took spoils. Then a group came after them, and ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾ was revealed.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, that some people came to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) in Kufa after the Battle of the Camel, and he said: "Distribute to them." He said: "This is the deprived."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, that a people in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) obtained booty, and then a group came later, and ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ was revealed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, saying: Amr related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "The deprived is the one who has no fay' (share of the public revenue) in Islam, and he is restricted (muharif) among the people."

⁕ [He] said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding his saying ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The deprived is the one to whom nothing of the fay' is allotted, and he is restricted (muharif) among the people."

Another said: He is the one whose wealth does not grow.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Husayn, who said: I asked Ikrima about "the beggar and the deprived." He said: "The beggar is the one who asks you, and the deprived is the one whose wealth does not grow."

Another said: He is the one whose fruit and crops have been destroyed.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The deprived is the one whose fruit and crops have been struck by calamity." He recited ﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who make it grow?﴾ … until ﴿Rather, we are deprived (mahrumun)﴾, and the companions of the Garden said: ﴿Indeed, we are astray. Rather, we are deprived﴾.

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding the words of Allah ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "That is not zakat, but it is what they spend from their wealth after paying zakat. The deprived is the one whose crops, fruit, or livestock offspring is struck by calamity, so he has a right over those Muslims who were not struck by that, just as the companions of the Garden said when Allah destroyed their garden: ﴿Rather, we are deprived.﴾" And he also said: ﴿If We willed, We would make it debris, and you would remain astonished. Indeed, we are laden with debt. Rather, we are deprived.﴾

It was al-Sha'bi who would say about this:

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Ibn Awn, who said: al-Sha'bi said: "I am unable to know what the deprived is."

The correct view on this matter, in my judgment, is that the deprived is the one who has been denied provision and is in need. This may be due to the loss of his wealth and crops, so that he becomes among those whom Allah has deprived of that; it may be due to his abstention and his refraining from asking; and it may be because he has no share in the spoils of war because he was absent from the battle. No view is more correct than that it be general, as the Exalted has said: ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ (17) ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾ (18) ﴿and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ (19)**

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil, the people of interpretation) differed over the meaning of His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾. Some said: its meaning is, "They used to be awake for little of the night, not sleeping," and they took "mā" (what) to carry the sense of negation.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They would wake up and pray between these two prayers, between Maghrib and 'Isha'."
- Zurayq ibn al-Shahhab narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, similarly.
- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Bukayr ibn Abi al-Samt narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They did not sleep until they had prayed the 'Atamah (night prayer)."
- They both said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Few were the nights that passed over them without their praying in them."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah said regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "Few were the nights that came upon them in which they did not pray to God, either from its beginning or from its middle."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "No night passed over them without their taking some portion of it, even if a little."
- He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "They would attain a portion of it."
- 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They did not sleep between Maghrib and 'Isha'."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam and Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They would attain a portion of the night."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Mutarrif, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Few were the nights that came over them without their sleeping through all of them."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They had little of the night in which they slept; they used to pray it."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Abi Najih say regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "They used to sleep little on any night until morning."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Little did they sleep on a night until morning; they did not perform tahajjud (voluntary night prayer)."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "They used to sleep but little of the night," and they treated the "mā" in His words ﴿mā yahja'ūn (they used to sleep)﴾ as a redundant particle (sila, a particle without independent meaning).

Those who said this include:

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "al-Hasan said: 'They endured the standing (prayer) of the night'."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: "They slept of it only a little."
- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from some of our companions, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They slept of the night only its least portion."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "Few were the nights that came over them without their sleeping."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "They did not sleep except a little."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said, reciting this verse ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: "I am not of the people of this verse."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "The standing (prayer) of the night."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: "They were energetic, so they extended (their prayer) until the pre-dawn."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "They extended (their) prayer and were energetic, until seeking forgiveness was at pre-dawn."
- He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: "They did not sleep at night except a little."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "al-Hasan and al-Zuhri used to say: 'They used to pray much of the night'." It is also permissible that the "mā" in this interpretation be in the nominative position (marfu', grammatical case), and the sense of the statement would be: "They used to sleep but little of the night, their sleep." As for the one who treats "mā" as a redundant particle, it has no grammatical position; the meaning of the statement according to his view would be "They used to sleep the little of the night," and if "mā" is redundant, then "qalīl" (little) is in the accusative case governed by "yahja'ūn" (they sleep).
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They did not sleep."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "They used to pray the 'Atamah," and in this interpretation, "mā" carries the sense of negation.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "A man from the people of Makkah said, Qatadah named him: the 'Atamah prayer."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: those good-doers were few among people before the obligations were prescribed upon them. They read the statement after His words ﴿Indeed they were before that good-doers﴾ as "They were few," and then began a new sentence with His words ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little﴾. Therefore, "mā" in this interpretation must carry the sense of negation.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He says: "The good-doers were few; then it begins, saying ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾," as He said ﴿And those who believed in God and His messengers, those are the truthful ones﴾, then He said: ﴿And the martyrs with their Lord; for them is their reward and their light﴾.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zubayr, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They were few among the people."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adiyy, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They were few among the people who did that."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adiyy, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They were few among the people at that time."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: "'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: God said ﴿Indeed the righteous are in gardens and springs﴾ ... to ﴿good-doers﴾." He said: "They were few." He means: "The good-doers were few." This is separated, then He resumed, saying ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little﴾.

As for His words ﴿yahja'ūn (they sleep)﴾, it means: they sleep; and al-hujū' (sleeping) is: sleep.

Those who held the view we have stated regarding this, among the interpreters, are:

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He says, "They sleep."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They sleep."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the same.
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿of the night they used to sleep but little﴾: "al-hujū' (sleep): sleep."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: He said, "They used to sleep little of the night." He said: "That is al-hajʻ (the dozing). And the Arabs say: 'When you travel, make us doze (ihja' bina) a little.'" He said: A man from the Banu Tamim said to my father: "O Abu Usamah, a description I do not find among us: God, blessed and exalted is He, mentioned a people and said ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾, and we, by God, stand little of the night." He said: My father said: "Blessed is the one who sleeps when he is drowsy, and whom God meets when he wakes."

The most correct of the interpretations regarding His words ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ is the view of the one who said: "They used to sleep but little of the night," because God, blessed and exalted is He, described them with that as praise for them and as commendation of them. So describing them with abundance of worship, staying awake through the night, and striving through it in what brings them near to Him and earns His pleasure is more fitting and more appropriate than describing them with little worship and much sleep. And what we have chosen in this is the most prevalent meaning according to the apparent sense of the revelation.

* *

And His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾.

The interpreters differed over its interpretation. Some said: its meaning is: "and at dawn they would pray."

Those who said this include:

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He says, "They would stand and pray." He says: "They used to stand and sleep." As God said to Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿Indeed your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) less than two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it, and a group of those with you﴾. This is sleep and this is standing. ﴿and a group of those with you﴾; likewise they would stand for a third, a half, and two-thirds. He says: they would sleep and they would stand.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He said, "They would pray."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He said, "They would pray."

Others said: Rather, what is meant is that they delayed their seeking forgiveness for their sins until the pre-dawn.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "They extended (their prayer) and were energetic, until seeking forgiveness was at pre-dawn."
- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾: He said, "They are the believers." He said: "It has reached us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) Ya'qub, when they asked him to seek forgiveness for them, (said) ﴿O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins﴾ — ﴿He said: I will seek forgiveness for you from my Lord﴾." He said: "Some people of knowledge said: he delayed the seeking of forgiveness until the pre-dawn." He said: "And some people of knowledge mentioned that the hour in which the gates of Paradise are opened is the pre-dawn."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say: "al-Sahar (pre-dawn) is the final sixth of the night."

* *

And His words ﴿and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: and in the wealth of these good-doers whose attributes He described there is a right for their beggar, the one who needs what is in their hands, and for the deprived.

The interpreters agreed with what we have said regarding the meaning of "the beggar," but they differed regarding the meaning of "the deprived." One said: it is the one who has been dispossessed (al-mahrūf), who has no share in Islam.

Those who said this include:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas: I asked him about "the beggar and the deprived," and he said: "The beggar is the one who asks people, and the deprived is the one who has no share in Islam, and he is mahrif (dispossessed)."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: He said: "The deprived: the mahraf (dispossessed)."
- Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The beggar: the beggar. And the deprived: the mahraf who has no share in Islam."
- Sahl ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The deprived: the mahraf who has no share in Islam."
- Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: He said: "The beggar: the one who asks. And the deprived: the mahraf."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Ishaq narrate from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, blessed and exalted is He, "the deprived": He said, "the mahraf."
- And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and the deprived﴾: "He is the man who is mahraf, who has no wealth except that which goes, which God has decreed for him."
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His words ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾, and he said: "The beggar: the one who asks. And the deprived: the mahraf who has no share in Islam."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Muqaddami narrated to me, saying: Quraysh ibn Anas narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: "The deprived: the mahraf (dispossessed)."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said regarding "the deprived": "He is the mahraf who has no one to show him kindness or give him anything."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Qilabah, who said: "A flood came in al-Yamamah and took the wealth of a man, so a man from among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'This is the deprived'."
- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Nafi', who said: "The deprived: the mahraf."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The deprived: the mahraf."
- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, from al-Walid ibn al-'Iza'r, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "The deprived: he is the mahraf."

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 51, verses 17–19 (part 2 of 2)**

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about "the deprived" (al-mahrum), and he did not say anything about it. Then Ata' said: He is the one who is restricted (al-mahdud al-muharif).

Another said: He is the one who abstains (al-muta'affif) and does not ask people for anything.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he was asked about "the deprived," and he said: "the muharif." [[هذا الأثر يناسب القول الأول، فلعله مؤخر من تقديم.]]

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "These are two of the poor of the Muslims: a beggar who asks with his hand, and a poor man who abstains. Both of them have a right over you, O son of Adam."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The beggar is the one who asks, and the deprived is the one who abstains and does not ask."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, saying: Ma'mar said, and al-Zuhri related to me, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one who is turned away by a date or two dates, or a morsel or two morsels." They said: "Then who is the poor man, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who does not find sufficiency, and whose need is not known so that he may be given charity. He is the deprived (al-mahrum)."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The beggar is the one who asks with his hand, and the deprived is the one who abstains. Both of them have a right over you, O son of Adam."

Another said: He is the one who has no share in the spoils of war (al-ghanima).

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent out a military expedition (sariyya), and they took spoils. Then a group came who had witnessed the spoils, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim al-Jadali, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, who said: An expedition was sent out and they took spoils. Then a group came after them, and ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾ was revealed.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, that some people came to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) in Kufa after the Battle of the Camel, and he said: "Distribute to them." He said: "This is the deprived."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, that a people in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) obtained booty, and then a group came later, and ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ was revealed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, saying: Amr related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "The deprived is the one who has no fay' (share of the public revenue) in Islam, and he is restricted (muharif) among the people."

⁕ [He] said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding his saying ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The deprived is the one to whom nothing of the fay' is allotted, and he is restricted (muharif) among the people."

Mention of those who said this:

Another said: He is the one whose fruit and crops have been destroyed.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "The deprived is the one whose fruit and crops have been struck by calamity." He recited ﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who make it grow?﴾ … until ﴿Rather, we are deprived (mahrumun)﴾, and the companions of the Garden said: ﴿Indeed, we are astray. Rather, we are deprived﴾.

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding the words of Allah ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾: "That is not zakat, but it is what they spend from their wealth after paying zakat. The deprived is the one whose crops, fruit, or livestock offspring is struck by calamity, so he has a right over those Muslims who were not struck by that, just as the companions of the Garden said when Allah destroyed their garden: ﴿Rather, we are deprived.﴾" And he also said: ﴿If We willed, We would make it debris, and you would remain astonished. Indeed, we are laden with debt. Rather, we are deprived.﴾

It was al-Sha'bi who would say about this:

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Ibn Awn, who said: al-Sha'bi said: "I am unable to know what the deprived is."

The correct view on this matter, in my judgment, is that the deprived is the one who has been denied provision and is in need. This may be due to the loss of his wealth and crops, so that he becomes among those whom Allah has deprived of that; it may be due to his abstention and his refraining from asking; and it may be because he has no share in the spoils of war because he was absent from the battle. No view is more correct than that it be general, as the Exalted has said: ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

And His words ﴿And in yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: And in the way of relieving yourselves, the excrement and urine, in yourselves there is a lesson for you and a proof for you of your Lord. Will you not see that in yourselves?

Those who said this:

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn al-Murtafiʿ, who said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: ﴿And in yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾ He said: the path of the excrement and urine.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafiʿ, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr ﴿And in yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾ He said: the way of relieving oneself and urine.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And in Allah's arranging the joints of your bodies and your limbs is proof for you that you were created to worship Him.

Those who said this:

Will you not then see?﴾, and he recited the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings dispersing﴾ [30:20], and said: And within us are many signs: this hearing, sight, tongue and heart, no one knows what it is, whether black or red; and this speech which one stammers with, and this heart, what is it, it is only a lump in the body, in which Allah places reason.
