⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it is the truth, just as [it is true] that you are speaking﴾, he said: "It has reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'May Allah fight against a people to whom their Lord swore by Himself, yet they did not believe Him.'" Al-Farra' said: Regarding the combination of "ma" and "inna" in this place, there are two aspects. The first: that this is like the Arabs' combining of two things, whether nouns or particles, as in the verse of the poet concerning nouns:

From the group of those who, the ones who, when... [the people of] the base of the door, the niggardly fear, they rattle [it]. [[This verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 311) that the Arabs may combine two nouns or particles when their wording differs, such as "allati" and "alladhina," which have one meaning, and one may substitute for the other, as in His words ﴿indeed it is the truth, just as [it is true] that you are speaking﴾, where He combined "ma" and "anna." The author has transmitted the remainder of al-Farra's discussion on the justification for combining these two forms. The grammarians cited it for the same purpose al-Farra' cited it. See the detailed discussion of the verse in al-Baghdadi's Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra (2: 529–534), where the verse is attributed to Abu al-Rubays al-Tha'labi. Its version, as in his poetry (in the Khizana, 532), is: "From the bright group, those who, when they gather... and the men fear the door-ring, so they rattle." It praises ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib, and he is the owner of the she-camel that Abu al-Rubays stole, and he praised its owner. Al-Jahiz related in al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin that the verses of which the verse of evidence is one were composed by a poet praising Usaylim ibn al-Ahnaf al-Asadi, saying: "He was possessed of eloquence, refinement, intellect and standing, and he is the one about whom the poet said..." the verses. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar said in Ansab Quraysh: Abu al-Rubays ʿAbbad ibn Tahfa al-Tha'labi said to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan... the verses, and among them the verse: "From the noble, lofty group, those who, when they set out... and the niggardly fear the door-ring, they rattle."]]

So he combined "alladhi" and "allati," and one of them substitutes for the other. And like the poet's words concerning particles:

"Never have I seen or heard of [anything] like today, [of] the mangy she-camels of a pursuer..." [[This verse is from the words of Duraid ibn al-Simmah, the knight of Jusham. He came to ʿAmr ibn al-Sharid al-Sulami to propose to his daughter al-Khansa', who used to coat his camels with tar against mange. When he saw her, he recited verses describing her, among them: "O Khunas, the heart has been enamored with you, and love's affliction has befallen it..."

When her father informed her of the purpose for which the knight of Jusham had come, she rejected him because of his old age and preferred her paternal cousins.

"Ma" is here verbal-masdarial, and likewise "inna" is a particle that makes what follows a masdar-type clause, and one of them suffices without the other.]]

So he combined "ma" and "inna," and both are negators, one of which can substitute for the other. As for the other aspect: if it were stated with "ma" alone, it would be a report that it is true, not false, and that is not what is meant. Rather, what is meant is: it is true, just as it is true that the human being speaks. Do you not see that your saying "Is your speech true?" means "Is it true or false?", while your saying "Is it true that you speak?" means a request for confirmation and nothing else; so "anna" was introduced to distinguish between the two meanings. He said: "This is the more wondrous of the two aspects to me."

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His words ﴿مِثْلَ مَا أَنَّكُمْ﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read ﴿مِثْلَ مَا﴾ in the accusative, meaning: "Indeed it is the truth, a certain truth," as if they took it in the direction of the masdar. It may also be that its accusative reading is because the Arabs put it in the accusative when they make the noun following it nominative, saying: "mithl man ʿabada Allah," "ʿAbd Allah mithluka," and "anta mithluhu," with "mithluhu" in both nominative and accusative. It may also be that its accusative reading is in the manner of the masdar: "indeed it is the truth, like your speaking." The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of Basra read it in the nominative, ﴿مِثْلُ مَا أَنَّكُمْ﴾, as an attribute (ṣifa) of "truth."

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are widely transmitted readings in the readings of the regions, close in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verse 24–26:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has the story of Abraham's honored guests reached you?﴿ (24) When they entered upon him and said, "Peace," he said, "Peace, [you are] a people unknown [to me]." (25) Then he went to his family and brought a fattened calf. (26)﴾

His mention, exalted is He, is addressed to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), informing him that He will bring down upon those among his people who persisted in their error and insisted on their disbelief, and did not repent of it, what He brought down upon the nations before them who had passed away. He is also admonishing his people from Quraysh by informing them of the accounts and stories of those (nations) and what was done to them. "Has the story of the honored guests of Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, reached you, O Muhammad?"

By His saying ﴿the honored﴾ He means that Abraham (peace be upon him) and Sarah served them with their own selves.

It was also said: the word ﴿the honored﴾ was used [because]

As related to us by Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿the honored guests of Abraham﴾: He said: Abraham honored them, and at that time he ordered his family to [prepare] the calf for them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿When they entered upon him﴾

It means: when Abraham's guests entered upon him, and they said to him, "Salaman" — that is, "We greet you with a greeting" — he said, "Salam."

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited ﴿salamun﴾ with an alif, in the sense that Abraham said to them, "Peace be upon you." The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited ﴿silmun﴾ without an alif, in the sense that he said, "You are a people [of] peace" (or "you are a strange people").

* *

As for His saying ﴿a people unknown﴾

It means: a people we do not know. "Qawmun munkarun" is in the nominative by an implied "antum" (you are).

* *

As for His saying ﴿Then he went to his family﴾

It means: he turned aside to his family and returned. Al-Farra' used to say: the verb "raagha" in this sense is not used unless its subject is concealing his going or coming. He said: Do you not see that you say "the people of Makkah have raagha," while you mean they returned or departed? So if the one returning concealed his return, "raagha" and "yarugh" would be appropriate for it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and brought a fattened calf﴾

It means: he brought his guests a fattened calf that he had roasted.

As related to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Then he went to his family and brought a fattened calf﴾: He said: most of the wealth of the Prophet of Allah Abraham (peace be upon him) was cattle.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verses 27–29:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So he brought it near to them, and said, "Will you not eat?"﴾ (27) ﴿Then he sensed fear of them. They said, "Do not fear." And they gave him good news of a knowing boy.﴾ (28) ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry, and struck her face, and said, "An old barren woman!"﴾ (29)

As for His saying, ﴿So he brought it near to them, and said, "Will you not eat?"﴾?

In the speech there is an omitted element, understood from the apparent context, which is: "So he brought it near to them, and they held back from eating it. Then he said, 'Will you not eat?'" ﴿Then he sensed fear of them﴾, meaning: Ibrahim sensed fear within himself from his guests, and concealed it. ﴿They said, "Do not fear," and they gave him good news of a knowing boy﴾, meaning: Ishaq. He said: "Alim" means "a knowing one" when he grows up. al-Farra' mentioned that some of the shaykhs used to say: if someone is expected to acquire knowledge, it is said: "Innahu la-'alim 'an qalil wa ghayah" (he is a scholar after a little while and an end); and in "al-sayyid" we say "sa'id" (a master), and "al-karim" we say "karim" (generous).

He said: "And what he said is good. This is also good Arabic speech, which Allah has used for 'alim, hakim and mayyit."

It was related from Mujahid concerning His saying ﴿a knowing boy﴾ that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿a knowing boy﴾: He said: Isma'il.

I only said that it refers to Ishaq, because the good news was of a child from Sarah, and Isma'il was from Hajar, not from Sarah.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry﴾:

It refers to Sarah. That coming forward was not a movement of relocation from one place to another, nor a transfer from one location to another; rather, it is like the saying of someone: "He came at me reviling me," meaning: he began to revile me.

* *

As for His saying ﴿in a loud cry﴾:

It means: in a cry (sayha).

The interpreters said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿in a loud cry﴾: he says: in a cry.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry, and struck her face﴾: by the "sarrah" he means the cry.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿in a loud cry﴾: he said: a cry.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry﴾: i.e., she came forward in a wail (ranna).

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿loud cry﴾: he said: she came forward wailing (tarunn). [[al-Ranna: a sorrowful cry. Wa rannat tarunnu rananan, wa arannat: she cried out.]]

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Karim al-Yami, from Ibn Sabat, concerning His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry﴾: he said: in a cry.

Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry﴾: he said: the "sarrah" is the cry.

I was informed from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿in a loud cry﴾: i.e., a cry. Some of them have said: that cry was "awwah," with a short alif.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾:

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of her striking (sakk) and the place on her face that she struck. Some of them said: the meaning of her striking her face is: slapping it.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾: he says: she slapped.

Others said: rather, she struck her forehead with her hand in wonder.

Mention of those who said that:

Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Gabriel gave Sarah the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub, she struck her forehead in wonder, and that is His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾: he said: her forehead.

Ibn Humayd told me, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Karim al-Yami, from Ibn Sabat, concerning His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾: he said: she did like this; and Sufyan struck his own forehead with his hand.

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿and struck her face﴾: she placed her hand on her forehead in wonder. The sakk, among the Arabs, is striking. It has also been said that her striking her face was that she joined her fingers and struck her forehead with them. ﴿And said, "An old barren woman!"﴾: meaning: she said, "Shall I bear a child?" The word "shall I bear" was omitted because the speech indicates it, and by the implied subject of "shall I bear," "old woman, barren" was made nominative. By "barren" is meant the one who does not bear.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Sulayman Abu Dawud related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mushash, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿an old barren woman﴾: he said: she does not bear.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: a man from the people of Khurasan from al-Azd, known as Abu Sasan, informed us, who said: I asked al-Dahhak about His saying ﴿barren﴾, and he said: the one who has no child.

As for His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry﴾:

It refers to Sarah. That coming forward was not a movement of relocation from one place to another, nor a transfer from one location to another; rather, it is like the saying of someone: "He came at me reviling me," meaning: he began to revile me.

* *

As for His saying ﴿in a loud cry﴾:

It means: in a cry (sayha).

The interpreters said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿in a loud cry﴾: he says: in a cry.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry, and struck her face﴾: by the "sarrah" he means the cry.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿in a loud cry﴾: he said: a cry.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry﴾: i.e., she came forward in a wail (ranna).

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿loud cry﴾: he said: she came forward wailing (tarunn). [[al-Ranna: a sorrowful cry. Wa rannat tarunnu rananan, wa arannat: she cried out.]]

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Karim al-Yami, from Ibn Sabat, concerning His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry﴾: he said: in a cry.

Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry﴾: he said: the "sarrah" is the cry.

I was informed from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿in a loud cry﴾: i.e., a cry. Some of them have said: that cry was "awwah," with a short alif.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾:

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of her striking (sakk) and the place on her face that she struck. Some of them said: the meaning of her striking her face is: slapping it.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾: he says: she slapped.

Others said: rather, she struck her forehead with her hand in wonder.

Mention of those who said that:

Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Gabriel gave Sarah the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub, she struck her forehead in wonder, and that is His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾: he said: her forehead.

Ibn Humayd told me, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Karim al-Yami, from Ibn Sabat, concerning His saying ﴿and struck her face﴾: he said: she did like this; and Sufyan struck his own forehead with his hand.

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿and struck her face﴾: she placed her hand on her forehead in wonder. The sakk, among the Arabs, is striking. It has also been said that her striking her face was that she joined her fingers and struck her forehead with them. ﴿And said, "An old barren woman!"﴾: meaning: she said, "Shall I bear a child?" The word "shall I bear" was omitted because the speech indicates it, and by the implied subject of "shall I bear," "old woman, barren" was made nominative. By "barren" is meant the one who does not bear.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Sulayman Abu Dawud related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mushash, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿an old barren woman﴾: he said: she does not bear.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: a man from the people of Khurasan from al-Azd, known as Abu Sasan, informed us, who said: I asked al-Dahhak about His saying ﴿barren﴾, and he said: the one who has no child.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verses 30–32:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿They said: "Thus has your Lord said. Indeed, He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing."﴾ [51:30] ﴿He said: "What is your business, O messengers?"﴾ [51:31] ﴿They said: "Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals."﴾ [51:32]

His, the Exalted's, remembrance says, reporting the speech of Abraham's guests when his wife spoke to them, after they had given her the good news of a knowing boy: "Shall I bear a child while I am an old woman, barren?" ﴿They said: "Thus has your Lord said"﴾ means: thus has your Lord said, that is, as we have informed you and told you. ﴿"Indeed, He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing"﴾. The pronoun in His words ﴿"Indeed, He"﴾ refers back to the Lord: He is the All-Wise in His management of His creation, the All-Knowing of their interests, and of what has been and what will be.

* *

It means: Abraham said to his guests: "What is your matter, O messengers?" ﴿They said: "Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals"﴾, who have committed transgression through their disbelief in Allah.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿That We may send down upon them stones of clay﴾ [51:33] ﴿marked by your Lord for those who transgress﴾ [51:34] ﴿Then We brought out those of the believers who were therein﴾ [51:35]

His words ﴿That We may send down upon them stones of clay﴾ mean: That We may rain down upon them from the sky stones of clay. ﴿Marked﴾ means: distinguished (mu'allamah).

As related:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿marked by your Lord for those who transgress﴾. He said: "The marked ones (al-musawwamah) are stones that were sealed; a stone would be white with a black spot in it, or a stone would be black with a white spot in it. That is their being marked with your Lord, O Ibrahim, for those who transgress," meaning for those who exceed the limits of Allah, the disbelievers in Him among the people of Lut. ﴿Then We brought out those of the believers who were therein﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We brought out those who were in the town of Sodom, the town of the people of Lut, from among the people of faith in Allah, and they were Lut and his two daughters. He referred to the town by His words ﴿those who were therein﴾, and this usage had not been applied to it before that.

* *

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And We found therein no house except one of the submitters [Muslims]﴾ [51:36] ﴿And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment﴾ [51:37]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We found in that town from which We brought out those who were in it of the believers no house other than one of the Muslims, and it was the house of Lut.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And We found therein no house except one of the Muslims﴾. He said: "Had there been more than that in it, Allah would have saved them, so that they would know that faith is preserved with Allah, and that its people are not lost."

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿And We found therein no house except one of the Muslims﴾: "These are the people of Lut; they found in it none except Lut."

Ibn 'Awf narrated to me, he said: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, he said: Safwan narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Muthanna and Muslim Abu al-Hayl al-Ash'ari narrated to us, saying: Allah said ﴿And We found therein no house except one of the Muslims﴾: Lut and his two daughters. He said: Then the punishment befell them. Allah said ﴿And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment﴾.

His words ﴿And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment﴾ mean: And We left in this town from which We brought out those of the believers who were in it a sign. He, may His praise be exalted, said ﴿And We left therein a sign﴾, and the meaning is: We left it as a sign, because it is the one that was overturned with its people, so it is the sign. This is like the speaker's saying: "You see in this thing a lesson and a sign," meaning: this thing is a sign and a lesson, just as He, may His praise be exalted, said ﴿Certainly there were in Joseph and his brothers signs for those who ask﴾ [12:7]. They themselves were the signs and their action was (the sign), and by "sign" is meant the admonition and lesson for those who fear the painful punishment of Allah in the Hereafter.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [We left a sign] in Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh with a clear authority.﴾ ﴿But he turned away with his supporters and said, "A sorcerer or a madman."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And [there is a sign] in Moses ibn 'Imran, when We sent him to Pharaoh with a proof that makes clear to whoever sees it that it is a proof for Moses of the truth of what he says and calls to.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿with a clear authority﴾: he said, "with a manifest excuse."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿but he turned away with his supporters﴾:

He says: Pharaoh turned away, as We sent Moses to him with his people, from among his soldiers and companions. The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said, although the wording of those who said it differs.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: My father narrated to me, who said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿It left nothing it came upon but that it made it like ashes﴾, he said: like a thing that is perishing.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿like ashes﴾, he said: like a thing that is perishing.

* Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿like ashes﴾: the rameem of trees.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿but that it made it like ashes﴾, he said: like the rameem of trees.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And in Thamud, when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a while." (43) But they defied the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on.﴾ (44)

His saying, exalted is He, means: And in Thamud too there is a lesson and a warning, when their Lord said to them, meaning: they became arrogant toward the command of their Lord and exalted themselves in haughty refusal to obey God.

And regarding His saying ﴿so the thunderbolt seized them﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: the thunderbolt of punishment seized them suddenly.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verses 45–46:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So they were not able to rise up, nor were they among those who could defend themselves﴾ [51:45] and ﴿And the people of Noah before—indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient﴾ [51:46].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: So they were not able to resist what came down upon them of the punishment of God, nor were they able to rise up against it.

As related to us:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿So they were not able to rise up﴾: he said: The people were not able to rise up against the punishment of God, blessed and exalted is He.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿So they were not able to rise up﴾, he said: from rising up.

Some of the people of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'arabiyyah) used to say: The meaning of His saying ﴿fa-ma istata'u min qiyam﴾ is: "fa-ma qamu bihā" (so they did not stand up to it). He said: If it were "fa-ma istata'u min iqamah" it would be correct, and the alif would be dropped from it, like His saying ﴿and He caused you to grow from the earth as a growth [nabatan]﴾ [71:17].

And His saying ﴿nor were they among those who could defend themselves﴾

He says: And they were not able to take retribution against those who inflicted upon them the punishment that befell them.

Qatadah used to say, regarding its interpretation: 

As related to us: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿nor were they among those who could defend themselves﴾, he said: They had no strength by which they could protect themselves from God, mighty and majestic is He.

And His saying ﴿and the people of Noah before—indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient﴾

The reciters differed in reading His saying ﴿wa-qawma Nuh﴾ in the accusative (naṣb). For the accusative there are several possibilities. One: that "the people" (al-qawm) is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with the pronoun in His saying ﴿so the thunderbolt seized them﴾ [51:44], since every destructive punishment the Arabs call "ṣāʿiqah" (thunderbolt); the meaning of the statement would then be: "the thunderbolt seized them and seized the people of Noah before." Two: that it is accusative by virtue of the sense of the statement, since what preceded of the reports of earlier nations serves as an indication of the intended meaning, and its meaning is: "We destroyed these nations, and We destroyed the people of Noah before." Three: that a verb governing it is supplied, so the meaning of the statement is: "Recount to them the people of Noah," as in His saying ﴿And Abraham, when he said to his people﴾ [29:16] and similar, meaning: inform them and recount to them. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read ﴿wa-qawmi Nuh﴾ with the genitive (khafḍ), on the sense: "and in the people of Noah," coordinating "the people" with "Moses" in His saying ﴿and in Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh﴾ [51:38].

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known readings among the readings of the cities (amṣār), so whichever reader recites it, he is correct. The interpretation of the reading in the genitive, "and in the people of Noah," also contains a lesson for them: We destroyed them before Thamud when they denied Our messenger Noah. ﴿Indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient﴾ means: they were opposing the command of God and departing from His obedience.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verse 47–48:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And the heaven We built with power, and indeed We are expanding it. And the earth — We spread it out, and how excellent are We as the Spreaders.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And the heaven — We raised it as a ceiling with power.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about that.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, ﴿And the heaven We built with power﴾: that is, "with strength."

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Mansur, that he said regarding this verse ﴿And the heaven We built with power﴾, he said: "with strength."

As for His words ﴿And indeed We are expanding it﴾

Ibn Zayd said regarding this:

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And indeed We are expanding it﴾, he said: "He expanded it, exalted is His majesty."

* * *

As for His words ﴿And the earth — We spread it out﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And the earth — We made it a bed for creation. ﴿And how excellent are We as the Spreaders﴾: meaning, how excellent are We as the Spreaders for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verse 49:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And of everything We created pairs, that you may remember﴾ (51:49).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We created of everything We created pairs, the first "We created" being omitted because the meaning of the speech points to it.

Scholars differed regarding the meaning of ﴿We created pairs﴾. Some said: It means: And of everything We created two different kinds, such as misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, and the like.

Mention of those who said that:

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj told us, saying: Mujahid said, regarding His saying ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾: "Disbelief and belief, misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, mankind and jinn."

Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Wazir told us, saying: Marwan ibn Muawiyah al-Fazari told us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾, he said: "The sun and the moon."

Others said: By the two pairs is meant: the male and the female.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾: "Male and female; those are the pair." And he recited ﴿and We made his wife fit for him﴾, and said: "His wife."

The most preferable of the two opinions on this matter is the view of Mujahid, namely that God, blessed and exalted, created for each of His creations a second that is opposite to it in meaning, so each of the two is a pair for the other; for this reason it was said: "We created pairs." Through this statement, may His majesty be exalted, He draws attention to His power to create whatever He wills of any thing, and that He is not like those things whose nature is to produce only one kind and not its opposite, for everything whose attribute is to produce one kind and not what is other than it, like fire whose nature is to heat and which is not fit for cooling, and like ice whose nature is to cool and which is not fit for heating, such a thing may not be described as perfect; perfection of praise belongs only to the One who is able to do whatever He wills among the different and the similar things.

* *

And His saying ﴿that you may remember﴾.

He says: So that you may remember and take heed by this, and thus know, O polytheists with God, that your Lord, who merits worship from you, is the One who is able to create a thing and its opposite, and to originate pairs of every thing, not one who is unable to do that.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner. (50) And do not set up with Allah another god. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.﴾ (51)

He, mentioned be His remembrance, says: Flee, O people, from the punishment of Allah to His mercy, by believing in Him, following His command, and acting in obedience to Him. ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner﴾ means: indeed, I am to you from Allah a warner, warning you of His punishment and making you fear His torment, which He brought down upon those peoples whose stories He has related to you, and which is what awaits them in the Hereafter.

* *

And His saying ﴿clear﴾

means: he makes his warning clear to you.

* *

And His saying ﴿And do not set up with Allah another god﴾

means, may His praise be exalted: And do not make, O people, with your Lord who created you another object of worship besides Him, for there is no object of worship deserving of worship other than Him. ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner﴾ means: indeed, I am to you, O people, a warner from His punishment for your worshipping a god other than Him, a clear warner who has made the warning plain to you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verse 52–53:

The explanation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿Thus, no messenger came to those before them but they said, "A magician or a madman!" Did they bequeath this saying to one another? Nay, they are a transgressing people.﴾

His Exalted remembrance says: Just as Quraysh denied their prophet Muhammad ﷺ and said, "He is a poet, or a magician, or a madman," so did the nations that denied their messengers, those upon whom God unleashed His vengeance, such as the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, Pharaoh and his people, do likewise. "Thus, there came not to those who came before them," meaning before these people of Quraysh, the people of Muhammad ﷺ, "any messenger but they said: a magician or a madman," just as Quraysh said to Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Did they bequeath this saying to one another? Nay, they are a transgressing people﴾:

His Exalted remembrance says: Did these deniers of Quraysh receive a charge from their forefathers and ancestors who passed before them, to deny Muhammad ﷺ regarding the truth he brought them, so that they accepted that from them?

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Did they bequeath this saying to one another?﴾ He said: The first of them charged the last of them with denial.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Did they bequeath this saying to one another﴾: That is, the first had charged the later with denial.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Nay, they are a transgressing people﴾:

His Exalted remembrance says: These polytheists did not charge their latter ones with that, but they are a people who exceed bounds and are rebellious against the command of their Lord, not obeying His command, nor refraining from what He has forbidden them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verses 54–55:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed (54), and remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers (55).﴾

His Exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "So turn away, O Muhammad, from these polytheists of Quraysh," meaning: "Withdraw from them until the command of God comes to you concerning them." It is said: "So-and-so turned away (wallā) from so-and-so" when he turned away from him and left him, as Husayn ibn Damdam said:

"As for the Banu 'Abs, their hybrid (hajīn) has turned away its horsemen, and escaped a'war (one who has failed)."

[The verse is by Husayn ibn Damdam. Abu 'Ubayda mentioned it in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 227b), saying at the words of His Exalted saying (fatawalla 'anhum), i.e. turn away from them and leave them. Husayn ibn Damdam said: "As for the Banu 'Abs ... [the verse]." Al-a'war: the one who is blinded (a'war) in that he did not fulfil his need and did not attain what he sought, and it is not from blindness of the eye.]

The a'war in this usage is the one who has failed, whose need was not fulfilled and who did not attain what he sought.

Those who relied on this interpretation of ours said the same as we have said. Those who said this are mentioned:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So turn away from them﴾: he said, "He withdrew from them."

And His saying ﴿So you are not to be blamed﴾

His majestic praise says: "So you are not to be blamed, O Muhammad; your Lord will not blame you for any negligence on your part in warning, for you have warned and conveyed what you were sent with."

Those who relied on this interpretation of ours said the same as we have said. Those who said this are mentioned:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿So turn away from them, so you are not to be blamed﴾: he said, "Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿So turn away from them, so you are not to be blamed﴾: "You have conveyed what We sent you with, so you are not to be blamed." He said: "And how would He blame him when he has discharged what he was commanded?"

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿So turn away from them, so you are not to be blamed﴾: It was mentioned to us that when this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and they thought that revelation had ceased and that punishment had drawn near. Then God, blessed and exalted, sent down afterward: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya informed us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Mujahid, who said: "'Ali came out wrapped in a cloak, covered with a mantle, and said: When ﴿So turn away from them, so you are not to be blamed﴾ was revealed, that grieved us, and we said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to turn away from us, until ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾ was revealed."

And His saying ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾

He says: "Admonish, O Muhammad, those to whom you were sent, for admonition benefits those who have faith in God."

As follows:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾: he said, "He admonished them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verses 56–57:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ (51:56).

The scholars of tafsir (exegesis) differed regarding the interpretation of His saying ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: I did not create the blessed among the jinn and mankind except for My worship, and the wretched among them for My disobedience.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾, he said: [it is] what they were created upon of wretchedness and happiness.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammil related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Zayd ibn Aslam, with something similar.

* Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil related to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Zayd ibn Aslam, with the like of it.

* Humayd ibn al-Rabi' al-Kharraz related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾, he said: He created them upon wretchedness and happiness.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾, he said: [it means] whoever was created for worship.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should submit to Me in servitude.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾: except that they should acknowledge servitude, willingly and unwillingly.

The most correct of the two opinions regarding this is the opinion we mentioned from Ibn Abbas, which is: I did not create the jinn and mankind except for Our worship and for humbling themselves to Our command.

If someone says: how then did they disbelieve, when He created them to humble themselves to His command? It is said: they have indeed humbled themselves to His decree which He decreed upon them, because His decree operates upon them, and they cannot resist it when it descends upon them. Only the one who disbelieved opposed Him in acting upon what He commanded him; as for humbling oneself to His decree, it is not something one can refuse.

* *

And His saying ﴿I do not want any provision from them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: I do not want from those whom I created of the jinn and mankind any provision that they provide for My creation, ﴿and I do not want that they feed Me﴾. He says: and I do not want from them any sustenance that they should sustain them, nor any food that they should feed them.

The people of tafsir have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿I do not want any provision from them, and I do not want that they feed Me﴾, he said: that they feed themselves.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verses 58–59:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, Possessor of strength, the Firm.﴾ (58) ﴿And indeed, for those who have wronged is a portion like the portion of their companions, so let them not ask Me to hasten.﴾ (59)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed Allah is the Provider of His creation, the One who guarantees their sustenance, Possessor of strength, the Firm.

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying ﴿al-matin﴾. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read it ﴿dhu al-quwwati al-matinu﴾ with a nominative ending (raf'), meaning: the Possessor of strength, the Mighty, so they made al-matin an adjective of dhu and applied it to the description of God. Yahya ibn Wthab and al-A'mash read it ﴿al-matini﴾ with a genitive ending (khafd), making it an adjective of quwwa (strength). Whoever read it in the genitive considered it permissible to make it an adjective of quwwa, though quwwa is feminine while al-matin is in the masculine form, because he took quwwa to mean the twisted, firmly-braided rope, so it is as if he said, according to this view: "the Possessor of a strong rope." Al-Farra' mentioned that some Arabs recited to him:

For every age I have worn garments
of a striped Yemeni cloth, bound...

[The verse is cited in Lisan al-Arab (thawb) and attributed to Ma'ruf ibn Abd al-Rahman. ... The verse is one of al-Farra's evidences in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, folio 313, where he said regarding the verse "Indeed Allah is the Provider, Possessor of strength, the Firm": Yahya ibn Wthab read "al-matin" in the genitive, making it an adjective of quwwa, even though it is feminine in form, because he had in mind the rope and the twisted thing. Some Arabs recited to me: "For every age..." the two verses. So he made al-mu'assab (the bound) an adjective of al-yumnah, which is feminine in form, because al-yumnah is a type and category of woven garments, so he took it in that sense. The people read "al-matin" in the nominative, as an attribute of God.]

Thus al-mu'assab is an adjective of al-yumnah, which is feminine in form, because al-yumnah is a type and category of garments, and so he took it in that sense.

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is ﴿dhu al-quwwati al-matinu﴾ with a nominative ending, as an attribute of God, may His majesty be exalted, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters is upon it; and if it were an adjective of quwwa, feminine form would have been more appropriate for it, although the masculine has its justification.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾: he said: the Mighty.

* *

As for His saying ﴿So indeed, for those who have wronged is a portion like the portion of their companions, so let them not ask Me to hasten﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: indeed for those who associated others with Allah among Quraysh and others is a portion (dhanub), which is a great bucket; it is also the sijl (large bucket) when it is filled or nearly filled. The word dhanub in this place is intended to mean share and portion. From this is the saying of Alqama ibn Abada:

And among every people you have dispensed favor,
so Shas has due a portion (dhanub) of your generosity.

[The verse is one of Abu Ubayda's evidences in Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 227, where he said regarding His saying "for those who have wronged is a portion (dhanub) like the portion of their companions": i.e., a share. Alqama ibn Abada said "And among every people you have dispensed..." ... The verse is from a long ode praising al-Harith ibn Abi Shamir al-Ghassani, who had captured his brother Shas, so he traveled seeking his release. ... The original meaning of dhanub is the bucket, and the intended meaning is share and portion. Abu Ubayda said: its origin is from the bucket; dhanub and sijl are the same, a bucket somewhat smaller.]

That is, a share, and its origin is what I mentioned. From it is the saying of the rajiz:

For us is a dhanub and for you a dhanub,
so if you refuse, then for us is the well (qalib).

[Dhanub: the sijl, which is less than a bucket; here it means share and portion. Qalib: the well. Al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, folio 313, regarding His saying "for those who have wronged is a portion (dhanub)": dhanub in the speech of the Arabs means a great bucket, but the Arabs take it to mean share and portion. With this the exegesis came: for those who have wronged is a share of punishment, as descended upon those before them. The poet said: "For us is a dhanub..." the two verses. Dhanub is both masculine and feminine.]

The meaning of the speech: indeed for those who have wronged is a share and portion of the punishment of Allah descending upon them, like the share of their companions who passed away before them from the nations, following their path of punishment, so let them not ask for it to be hastened.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for those who have wronged is a portion﴾: he said: a bucket.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for those who have wronged is a portion like the portion of their companions﴾: he said: He says, for those who have wronged is a punishment like the punishment of their companions, so let them not ask for it to be hastened.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿a portion like the portion of their companions﴾ "so let them not ask to hasten": a sijl of punishment.

- He said: Affan ibn Muslim told us, saying: Shihab ibn Su'ayra told us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿a portion like the portion of their companions﴾: a bucket like the bucket of their companions.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿dhanuban﴾: he said: a sijl.

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿for those who have wronged is a portion﴾: a sijl of the punishment of Allah.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿for those who have wronged is a portion like the portion of their companions﴾: he said: a punishment like the punishment of their companions.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿for those who have wronged is a portion like the portion of their companions﴾: he said: it means a portion of punishment; he said: a sijl of the punishment of Allah is said to them, and this was done to their companions before them, so for them is a punishment like the punishment of their companions, so let them not ask to hasten.

- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿a portion like the portion of their companions﴾: he said: a share of the punishment.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿a portion like the portion of their companions﴾ "so let them not ask to hasten": a sijl of punishment.

- He said: Affan ibn Muslim told us, saying: Shihab ibn Su'ayra told us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿a portion like the portion of their companions﴾: a bucket like the bucket of their companions.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿dhanuban﴾: he said: a sijl.

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿for those who have wronged is a portion﴾: a sijl of the punishment of Allah.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿for those who have wronged is a portion like the portion of their companions﴾: he said: a punishment like the punishment of their companions.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿for those who have wronged is a portion like the portion of their companions﴾: he said: it means a portion of punishment; he said: a sijl of the punishment of Allah is said to them, and this was done to their companions before them, so for them is a punishment like the punishment of their companions, so let them not ask to hasten.

- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿a portion like the portion of their companions﴾: he said: a share of the punishment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 51, verse 60:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve, from their day which they are promised.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: So the flowing valley in Hell, of pus and putrid matter, is for those who disbelieve in Allah and deny His oneness, from their day in which they are promised the descent of Allah's punishment when it descends upon them, and what suffering and hardship they will meet therein.

End of the commentary on Surah adh-Dhariyat.
